arbonet_wnv_blood_donors.short_name: West Nile presumptive viremic blood donors
arbonet_wnv_blood_donors.long_name: West Nile virus presumptive viremic blood donors identified by blood donor screening
arbonet_wnv_blood_donors.short_description: Presumptive viremic blood donors identified through West Nile virus blood donor screening.
arbonet_wnv_blood_donors.long_description: Count of presumptive viremic blood donors, defined by CDC as people who had no symptoms at the time of donating blood but whose blood tested positive when screened for West Nile virus. Identified through blood supply screening rather than clinical care, so counted separately from reported human disease cases. Reported for West Nile virus only, as it is the only one of ArboNET's arboviruses with routine blood donor screening.
arbonet_wnv_blood_donors.name: arbonet_wnv_blood_donors

info.short_name: West Nile virus presumptive viremic blood donors
info.long_name: West Nile virus presumptive viremic blood donors identified by blood donor screening
info.short_description: Presumptive viremic blood donors identified through West Nile virus blood donor screening.
info.long_description: Count of presumptive viremic blood donors, defined by CDC as people who had no symptoms at the time of donating blood through a blood collection agency but whose blood tested positive when screened for the presence of West Nile virus. Some presumptive viremic donors go on to develop symptoms after donation. These donors are identified through blood supply screening rather than clinical care, so they are counted separately from the reported human disease cases and are not a subset of them. This measure is reported for West Nile virus only, as it is the only one of these six arboviruses for which routine blood donor screening is conducted.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} West Nile virus presumptive viremic blood donors were identified in {time}.

arbonet_wnv_blood_donors.short_description: Presumptive viremic blood donors identified through West Nile virus blood donor screening.
arbonet_wnv_blood_donors.long_description: Count of presumptive viremic blood donors, defined by CDC as people who had no symptoms at the time of donating blood but whose blood tested positive when screened for West Nile virus. Identified through blood supply screening rather than clinical care, so counted separately from reported human disease cases. Reported for West Nile virus only, as it is the only one of ArboNET's arboviruses with routine blood donor screening.

info.short_description: Presumptive viremic blood donors identified through West Nile virus blood donor screening.
info.long_description: Count of presumptive viremic blood donors, defined by CDC as people who had no symptoms at the time of donating blood through a blood collection agency but whose blood tested positive when screened for the presence of West Nile virus. Some presumptive viremic donors go on to develop symptoms after donation. These donors are identified through blood supply screening rather than clinical care, so they are counted separately from the reported human disease cases and are not a subset of them. This measure is reported for West Nile virus only, as it is the only one of these six arboviruses for which routine blood donor screening is conducted.
info.statement: In {location}, {value} West Nile virus presumptive viremic blood donors were identified in {time}.

bundle_vector_borne/dist/vector_borne.pa.short_description: Value for the vector-borne disease measure identified by the measure column: annual case/activity counts as reported to ArboNET (national, state, and county), or weekly case counts for the NNDSS measures (national and state only). NNDSS publishes cumulative year-to-date counts; this bundle de-cumulates them into weekly incident counts by differencing consecutive weeks within each MMWR year, so occasional negative values reflect downward revisions to the source's cumulative totals.

arbonet.name: ArboNET Arboviral Disease Surveillance System
arbonet.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Division of Vector-Borne Diseases
arbonet.description: ArboNET is the national arboviral surveillance system managed by CDC together with state and territorial health departments. In addition to human disease, ArboNET maintains data on arboviral infections among presumptive viremic blood donors, veterinary disease cases, mosquitoes, dead birds, and sentinel animals. Human cases are reported by county of residence rather than location of exposure, and are assigned to the year of illness onset. Several caveats apply: under-reporting is inherent to any surveillance system that depends on clinicians suspecting the disease, ordering the appropriate test, and reporting confirmed results; non-neuroinvasive cases are substantially more under-reported than neuroinvasive cases, so total case counts should not be used to compare disease activity between locations or over time; and there is a lag in reporting to CDC. Connecticut reported by county through 2022 and by planning region from 2023 onward, so its geography codes change mid-series. Reporting years differ by disease and the most recent year is preliminary and subject to change.
arbonet.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.

nnds.name: National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System (NNDSS)
nnds.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
nnds.description: The National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System (NNDSS) is a nationwide collaboration that enables all levels of public health to share notifiable disease related health information. Public health uses this information to monitor, control, and prevent the occurrence and spread of state-reportable and nationally notifiable infectious and some non-infectious diseases and conditions. NNDSS publishes weekly cumulative year-to-date case counts; this bundle de-cumulates them (by differencing consecutive weeks within each MMWR year) into weekly incident counts covering vector-borne, tick-borne, and travel-associated arboviral and parasitic diseases: the eight ArboNET-overlapping arboviral diseases NNDSS also tracks by weekly provisional count (chikungunya, Eastern/Western equine encephalitis, Jamestown Canyon, La Crosse, Powassan, St. Louis encephalitis, and West Nile virus disease), babesiosis, dengue and dengue-like illness, ehrlichiosis/anaplasmosis, malaria, and non-congenital Zika virus disease. Negative values in case counts reflect retroactive corrections by the CDC.
nnds.restrictions: Public domain. CDC data is generally not subject to copyright restrictions.
